newsitem.title: USA: Sheldahl sees Q3 loss of $0.18 share.
newsitem.headline: Sheldahl sees Q3 loss of $0.18 share.

text.p: Sheldahl Inc said Thursday it expects to report a loss of about $0.18 a share for the third quarter due to the impact of several strikes in the automotive industry.
Analysts had expected the company to report a loss of $0.08 per share, Sheldahl said.
Sheldahl, which makes products for the automotive electronics and datacommunications markets, said its results were negatively impacted by strikes at General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp.

It expects third-quarter revenues to be in the range of $28.5 million to $29.0 million, or about $1.5 million to $2.0 million below expectations, it said. The majority of the decline is automotive-related.
In addition to problems in the auto industry, Sheldahl said it has experienced increased costs at its Micro Products facility.

"The timing of the Chrysler and General Motors strikes has had an unsettling impact on our shipping schedules recently, and indications are that this effect is likely to continue through the end of the month. We are working closely with our suppliers to ensure that inventory levels are properly maintained in order to minimize potential near-term strike-related volatility," said Said James E. Donaghy, Sheldahl's president and chief executive.

"Product qualification and production ramp-up at Sheldahl's Micro Products facility in Longmont, Colo., continue with great intensity and focus. We have commenced volume production to allow us to be in a position to rapidly respond as orders build. In the short run, this effort increases costs, but is entirely appropriate based on market conditions," Donaghy said.

"Micro product design activity continues to accelerate as industry demand in the rapid-growth ball grid array integrated circuits sector builds and current customers work to upgrade their assembly lines to handle our substrate," he added.
